author: Haroon Siddique Legal affairs correspondent
description:
Polling for rights group shows issue is concern for voters and many feel recent policies have had negative effect

Free speech will be a big concern for voters at the next general election, with the government’s current approach on the issue perceived by many to be bad for Britain, polling suggests.

Three in five people said a political party’s position on free speech would affect how they voted at a general election. The human rights organisation Liberty, which commissioned the polling from More in Common, claimed the results showed that Labour’s failure to protect free speech could cost it votes.

Continue reading...
title: Failure to protect free speech could cost Labour votes at next election, says Liberty

author: Agence France-Presse
description:
• Americans dominate final day singles contests

  • US president gives speech before final day

The United States made a stunning rally to capture an 11th consecutive Presidents Cup title on Sunday, completing a 17-13 victory over the Internationals with Donald Trump in attendance.

Jacob Bridgeman secured the clinching point at Medinah by sinking a four-foot par putt at the 18th hole to defeat Australian Min Woo Lee 1-up.

Continue reading...
title: Snedeker says Trump ‘gets all the credit’ after US complete huge Presidents Cup comeback

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
Couple was seriously injured after attack on 19 September and are mourning the death of their French bulldog

A bear attack last weekend has left a California couple seriously injured and mourning the death of their French bulldog, who tried to protect them from the animal.

In the early hours of 19 September, Jeff Wilson, who lives in rural northern California, let his dog Cassie go outside, the San Francisco Chronicle reported.

Continue reading...
title: Dog dies trying to protect northern California couple from bear attack

author: Associated Press
description:
Vučić not allowed to seek third presidential term and PM election will test his grip on rule after widespread protests

Serbia’s populist president, Aleksandar Vučić, has resigned to pursue an attempt to become the prime minister in an upcoming early parliamentary election that will test his firm rule in the Balkan country after nearly two years of protests.

Vučić’s second presidential term would otherwise end in May next year. He is banned by the Serbian constitution from seeking a third term and said he was resigning to lead his rightwing Serbian Progressive party (SNS) in the 25 October ballot.

Continue reading...
title: Serbia’s populist president Aleksandar Vučić resigns to run for prime minister

author: Hannah J Davies
description:
It’s light stuff with more than a touch of Emily in Paris to it, but the actor’s latest travelogue has enough passion to make it highly endearing TV

‘I’m Eva Longoria and I’m a SERIOUS Francophile!” So begins each instalment of the actor’s Gallic travelogue. France, says Longoria, “is my home away from home”, although she’s usually in the country for work, rather than to experience its abundance of “joie de vivre”. (She does, she notes, have some extracurricular experience with the French, having previously been married to the French-American basketball player Tony Parker for three years.) Now, though, she is on her own adventure, having returned to l’Hexagone for something “deeper”. Cut to a clip of our intrepid guide in a vineyard, getting acquainted with cabernet sauvignon grapes (“That’s my favourite!” she whispers animatedly), before we segue to her floating gracefully past the Eiffel Tower.

Eva Longoria: Searching for France follows the equally a
title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France review – this lovely travel show radiates charm

author: Pippa Crerar, Alexandra Topping and Kiran Stacey
description:
PM says he is willing to expend political capital to bring in universal service that would be funded by ‘everybody’

  • Analysis: can Labour hang on to Burnham bounce?

Andy Burnham will fight the next election with a pledge to finally fix the broken social care system, acknowledging that he is willing to expend political capital by asking taxpayers to cover the cost.

As Labour’s party conference began in Liverpool, he pledged to “rip the plaster off” to radically transform care, setting out a vision for a universal service that would be free at the point of use for everybody in England.

Continue reading...
title: Andy Burnham to fight next election with plan for NHS-style care service

author: Jamie Grierson, Vikram Dodd and Helena Horton
description:
Counter-terrorism police investigate whether Iran is behind suspected bomb plot after member of public calls 999 over suspicious vehicles

Counter-terrorism police are investigating whether Iran is behind a suspected bomb plot after armed officers found explosives on three vans parked minutes from an RAF base used by the US military.

The Guardian understands that after five men were arrested on terrorism charges, investigators were examining materials found in the vans, with an initial view being they were consistent with improvised explosive devices.

Continue reading...
title: Five arrested on terrorism charges after explosives found near RAF base used by US

author: John Brewin
description:
• Updates from 7.45pm BST kick-offs in Nations League

  • Live scores | Email John | And follow us over on TikTok

Full-time scores from the earlier Nations League matches:

Lithuania 1-1 Azerbaijan

Austria 3-1 Kosovo

Denmark 2-0 Wales

Gibraltar 0-0 Andorra

Serbia 1-2 Netherlands

title: Israel v Republic of Ireland, Norway v Portugal, Germany v Greece: Nations League – live

author: Reuters
description:
• Bavuma and Miller smash centuries in second ODI

  • Australia batters fall 32 runs short despite strong start

Temba Bavuma and David Miller both struck centuries as South Africa defeated Australia by 32 runs in the ⁠second one-day international in Johannesburg, securing victory in the three-match series with a game to spare.

Australia sent their hosts in to bat and South ⁠Africa amassed 365 for ⁠nine in their ​50 overs, before bowling the visitors out for 333 in 49.5 overs to win a high-scoring encounter. The Proteas continued their recent dominance over their rivals with a 19th ODI ⁠win in their last 25 meetings.

Continue reading...
title: South Africa power to ODI series win as Australia’s middle order struggles again

author: Tumaini Carayol at the O2 Arena
description:
• Jakub Mensik and Flavio Cobolli win doubles 7-5, 6-3

  • Andre Agassi goads Alexander Zverev at ceremony

Team Europe reclaimed their Laver Cup title with a dominant 13-5 victory against Team World on the final day of competition at the O2 Arena.

The contest had been finely poised after two days’ play, with Team Europe holding a narrow 7-5 lead at the beginning of the day. With each match worth three points on Sunday, Europe needed two victories out of the four remaining matches to win. They clinched their victory efficiently.

Continue reading...
title: Alexander Zverev clinches Laver Cup for Team Europe with victory over Learner Tien

author: Graham Searles
description:
• Live updates from the 6pm BST games around the NFL

  • Get in touch: mail Graham about all the latest matches

Some big news today is Super Bowl winning quarterback Sam Darnold returning for the Seattle Seahawks. Drew Lock deputised in style with good wins over the Patriots and Cardinals but the main man returns from a glute injury to face the winless Washington Commanders.

There are no layups in the NFL but, with Washington missing their star QB Jayden Daniels, the pressure won’t be quite so high on Darnold to come out swinging for the fences. He can rely on arguably the NFL’s best defense to shutdown Commanders backup passer Marcus Mariota and keep it conservative through the air. Though hopefully he will still let a few bombs go to Jaxon Smith-Njigba.
title: NFL week three: Chiefs at Dolphins, Chargers at Bills, Patriots at Jaguars, and more – live

author: Rowena Mason and Pippa Crerar
description:
Pat McFadden urges Labour MPs to back overhauls, amid signs party looking to cut payments for some 16- to 24-year-olds

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Labour MPs have a moral responsibility to accept significant changes to the welfare system to help get more young people into work, the work and pensions secretary has said.

In a sign he is looking to overhaul the welfare state, Pat McFadden said it was time for Labour to “renew” the system first created by the Clement Attlee government and given a new deal by New Labour.

Continue reading...
title: Changing UK benefits for young people a ‘moral crusade’, says minister

author: Edward Helmore
description:
Waltz says Trump rejected Iran’s proposal to end war because they ‘were asking for everything up front’

The Trump administration’s ambassador to the United Nations said the US rejected Iran’s proposal to end the ongoing war there because Iranian negotiators “were asking for everything up front”.

Echoing comments by Donald Trump on Saturday, the president’s UN ambassador Mike Waltz told CNN’s State of the Union on Sunday that Iran had asked for relief “from billions and billions of sanctions that are going into place” as part of an economic blockade on Iran. The blockade is aimed at putting pressure on Iran to stop its attacks ‌on vessels in the strait of Hormuz.

Continue reading...
title: UN ambassador Waltz says Iran was not negotiating ‘in good faith’ to end war

author: Editorial
description:
If a guilty verdict on multiple counts of financial misreporting is upheld against the club, its achievements in the modern era will be forever tainted

In surveys ranking the Premier League’s greatest moments, football supporters regularly give pride of place to Sergio Agüero’s championship-winning goal for Manchester City in 2012. Scored in injury time on the last day of the season, Agüero’s strike against Queens Park Rangers delivered the first league title for City since the 1960s. Knocking their historic rivals Manchester United into second place, it also signalled a new era in which the club replaced United as the dominant force in the English game.

“Aguerooooooo!” – the incredulous single-word response from the match commentator Martin Tyler – has entered football folklore. But an asterisk may now be needed at the end of all those Os.
title: The Guardian view on Manchester City: a strange kind of glory | Editorial

author: Joanna Partridge
description:
Keys crops such as cereals, potatoes, sugar and oils grown in areas with moderate to very high risk

The vast majority of the UK’s essential foods, including cereals, potatoes, sugar and oil, are grown in areas of England rated as having a moderate to very high risk of drought.

A very high proportion – 81% – of England’s fresh produce is concentrated in parts of the country that are already experiencing water stress, according to the analysis by nature-focused investment fund Rebalance Earth.

Continue reading...
title: Most of UK’s essential food supply grown in drought-risk areas, report warns

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
At least one person killed and nearly 150,000 households lost electricity from North Carolina to New England

A strong, deadly storm known as a nor’easter battered the US’s east coast over the weekend, bringing power outages, flooding, damaging winds and hazardous ocean conditions.

Trees and power lines were knocked down across the region, at least one person was killed and hundreds of thousands were left without electricity as officials cautioned that conditions could deteriorate further.

Continue reading...
title: Nor’easter storm batters US east coast with heavy winds and power outages

author: Keren Landman
description:
Experts share what you need to know about GLP-1-related hair loss as the side-effect gets more attention from researchers

About 20 million people across the US, UK, and EU are taking GLP-1 receptor agonists like tirzepatide and semaglutide (Ozempic or Mounjaro are common brands) for weight loss and type 2 diabetes. As their use has surged, we’re learning more about their side-effects. One that’s been getting a lot of attention from researchers lately: hair loss.

In one survey of people who take these medications, 20% of respondents experienced hair shedding, although the lack of high-quality data from a randomized, controlled trial to assess this side-effect makes it difficult to know exactly how
title: Does GLP-1 use result in significant hair loss?

author: Jack Snape
description:
One year from a home World Cup, in circumstances comically heroic, this was the match Australia needed

With four minutes to go, and four players down, Australia lead by two tries against the world champions in Perth. The Wallabies have been unbeaten in four matches under new coach Les Kiss, but they have not yet been tested against a rugby power. If they were looking for a test, this is now it.

On the arena where the men’s rugby World Cup will begin in just over one year, Australia are showing promise. They had led South Africa 42-17 midway through the second half. Now, the score is 42-31.

Continue reading...
title: The four minutes that lasted a lifetime as Wallabies won all-time chaos classic | Jack Snape

author: Chloe Mac Donnell
description:
The late designer’s niece echoes his sense of relaxation, as the house seeks to prove itself to potential buyers

A year after the death of Giorgio Armani, the Italian fashion house he founded in 1975 is facing increasing uncertainty about its future ownership.

In his will, Armani, who ruled over the business for 50 years, instructed his heirs to sell an initial 15% stake of the company within 18 months of his death. If a private sale does not materialise, an IPO is mandated to take place. Now there are reports the group is readying itself for formal talks with the French conglomerate LVMH, the beauty giant L’Oréal and the eyewear group EssilorLuxottica – three of Armani’s preferred acquirers – over the possible sale of a minority stake.

Continue reading...
title: With turbulence all around, Armani plays it safe and easy in Milan

author: Jennifer Rankin
description:
70% vote against tightening centuries-old neutrality, which far right said was eroded by sanctions against Russia

Swiss voters have decisively rejected a proposal for a strict definition of neutrality that would have required Switzerland to curb cooperation with Nato and abandon sanctions against Russia.

All cantons and about 70% of voters rejected the proposal for a strictly defined version of neutrality to be ⁠written into the Swiss constitution, final results from the Federal Statistical Office showed. The motion had been promoted by the far-right Swiss People’s party (SVP).

Continue reading...
title: Swiss voters reject stricter neutrality rules that would curb Nato cooperation

author: Jamie Jackson
description:
• Manchester City won match 1-0 after goal by Yaya Touré

  • Club deny wrongdoing and say ‘process is ongoing’

Tony Pulis has said his Stoke City team was “cheated” out of the 2011 FA Cup after Manchester City were found guilty on virtually all counts of breaching Premier League financial rules.

Pulis’ Stoke lost the 2011 Cup final 1-0 after Yaya Touré’s strike. Yet following Friday’s news that City are guilty on all but one of the more than 100 charges laid by the Premier League in February 2023, Pulis feels serious discontent. City are expected to appeal and they deny any wrongdoing.
title: Tony Pulis says he and Stoke ‘were cheated’ in 2011 FA Cup final after Manchester City verdict

author: Lydia, as told to Katie Cunningham
description:
My son adores helicopters, so we waved as hard as possible as it flew past. Then it suddenly looped and came back around

  • Read more in the kindness of strangers series

My sister lives in Ukraine; I live in Australia. We had gone five long years without seeing each other when we finally reunited during a trip to Los Angeles. One day we took my three-year-old son to the beach and spent the afternoon catching up.

We had a lot of conversations about people and kindness that day. I told her how I had noticed a softer side to men since having a son. As a woman, you’re often wary of construction workers, for example – what might they say to me when I walk past? But now when I pass a building site with my son, the workers often let him play with their radio, or beep a tractor to make him laugh. It was very heartwarming and gave me a whole new perspective on the other sex.<
title: The kindness of strangers: Two helicopter pilots flew down low to wave to my three-year-old son – he was beside himself with joy

author: Tom Gauld
description: Continue reading...
title: Tom Gauld on the author simulator – cartoon

author: Bianca Denny
description:
These one-sided connections with famous people are a normal part of modern life. But sometimes they can lead to emotional distress

  • The modern mind is a column where experts discuss mental health issues they are seeing in their work

“It came as such a shock. I just can’t believe he’s gone.”

Psychologists are accustomed to seeing bereaved individuals. But working with Jodie* presented a unique challenge – she’d never met the person she was grieving. Jodie was reeling after the recent death of a well known singer. Despite not knowing the singer personally, Jodie’s grief and loss seemed as palpable as other patients speaking about the deaths of family members or loved ones. Jodie reported that weeks after the singer’s death, she was struggling to attend work and was sleeping poorly, describing herself as consumed with thoughts of the singer.
title: When a celebrity dies, it can feel like losing a loved one. Why do we get so invested in parasocial relationships? | Bianca Denny

author: Linda Geddes
description:
Scientists are racing to understand how fires behave as hotter summers turn green landscapes into tinderboxes

From the scorched heathlands of the New Forest to the smouldering valleys of south Wales and burned-out homes in Stourbridge, an extraordinary summer of wildfires has left its mark across Britain.

To most of us, these charred landscapes may look like pure devastation, but to a trained wildfire investigator they are full of clues. Heat-scorched leaves can become frozen in position, preserving evidence of the wind direction as the fire passed through. Soot or staining on roc
title: Anatomy of an inferno: inside the push to map, predict and prevent spread of increasing UK wildfires

author: Sara Braun
description:
The Guardian spoke with surrogates across the US about what they think of the controversy surrounding the practice

Surrogacy has been thrust into the national spotlight in recent weeks, with both the announcement of Lena Dunham using a surrogate to start a family and the ongoing legal battle surrounding McKenna West, a gestational surrogate who fled to Texas to avoid having an abortion that was requested by the child’s biological parents.

With a renewed public interest on commercial, or compensated, surrogacy, the Guardian spoke with surrogates across the US who shared their experiences and how they feel about surrogacy being part of a global, public conversation.

Continue reading...<
title: ‘I wanted to help another family’: four surrogates on how they feel about the surrogacy discourse

author: Harriet Gibsone
description:
The Grammy-winning artist on ​d​estroying egos in school, the dealers who looked out for her, and learning from early failure

Born Eve Jihan Jeffers in Philadelphia in 1978, rapper Eve released her debut album, Let There Be Eve … Ruff Ryders’ First Lady, in 1999; it entered the Billboard 200 at No 1. She followed its success with the platinum-selling Scorpion, which went on to win a Grammy for the single Let Me Blow Ya Mind. As an actor, she appeared in the Barbershop films and starred in her own sitcom, Eve. She married London-based entrepreneur Maximillion Cooper in 2014; together they have a son, and she is stepmother to his four children. Eve will tour the UK and Europe in 2027.

This was taken in Miami, where I was recording Scorpion. I was obsessed with red because of its astrological affiliation with Scorpio – everything had to be that colour. My hair is short because I convinced my hairstylist to put both a perm relaxer a
title: Rapper and actor Eve looks back: ‘I was the only girl in the boardroom in major label meetings – that Philly girl had to come out’

description:
The long-running series in which readers answer other readers’ questions on subjects ranging from trivial flights of fancy to profound scientific and philosophical concepts

  • This week’s question: Is it possible that 3 is the most common number in UK street addresses?

It’s clear that the world as it is – considering the climate crisis, the rise of nationalism, geopolitical tumult, the possibility of AI killing us all by the end of the decade – could do with some more ethically astute and capable leadership. If you could time warp them into the present day, which leader from history could the world do with now – and why? Bernard, Machynlleth

Send new questions to
title: Readers reply: Which leader from history does the world need now?

author: Jennifer Rankin
description:
Catholic church must reckon with its ‘painful errors’, pontiff tells crowd in Lourdes during four-day tour

The pope has called on the Catholic church to heal “deep wounds” and “painful errors”, before a meeting with survivors of child sexual abuse as he continues his four-day visit to France.

Addressing a crowd in a large field near the Catholic shrine of Lourdes on Sunday, Pope Leo XIV called on the church to reckon with its past, without directly referencing sexual abuse scandals in France that affected at least 330,000 children over seven decades.

Continue reading...
title: Pope Leo urges healing of ‘deep wounds’ before meeting child sexual abuse survivors in France

author: Angus Fontaine
description:
• Australia beat South Africa 42-38 in World Cup warning

  • Les Kiss’s side reduced to 11 men in final 15 minutes

A year out from the World Cup, Australia have sent a huge warning shot to the competition, upsetting the two-time trophy winners South Africa with an extraordinary 42-38 win in Perth. On a weekend when the AFL and NRL delivered fairytale comebacks, the Wallabies trumped both rival codes, hammering rugby’s No 1 team with a skilful display that ended in bizarre circumstances when the men in gold held on despite being reduced to 11 players at the end.

Fittingly, the victory found the Wallabies harnessing the aerial powers of Australian Rules and the rambunctious power of rugby league to dominate rugby’s world champions with a brilliant, inventive and courageous five-try performance that kept alive new coach Les Kiss’s unbeaten record and breathed new hope into the hearts of Australian fans nationwide.
title: Wallabies hold off world champion Springboks in chaotic Test for the ages

author: Guardian sport and agencies
description:
• Senior able to move limbs but taken to hospital

  • USC linebacker Desman Stephens II ejected for play

Oregon head coach Dan Lanning has decried a “disgusting play” that left his starting quarterback, Dante Moore, in hospital during the Ducks’ 41-27 win over USC.

Moore was carted off the field after a late hit by Trojans linebacker ⁠Desman Stephens II in the first half of Saturday’s game in Los Angeles. He was able to move his fingers and ⁠feet and rotate his arms, and was taken to Los Angeles General Medical Center, according to the NBC broadcast. An Oregon spokesperson later ⁠said that Moore had movement in all of his extremities and was ​being evaluated.

Continue reading...
title: Lanning decries ‘disgusting’ late hit that sends Oregon QB Dante Moore to hospital

author: Lisa O’Carroll Senior correspondent
description:
Home Office faces legal action after 1,473 people living in UK before Brexit told settled status was granted in error

The Home Office is facing legal action over a controversial policy to strip EU citizens who were in the UK before Brexit of their residency rights on the grounds that it gave them the status “in error”.

It comes as a Home Office minister revealed that the government has contacted 1,473 citizens with post-Brexit residency rights to tell them the original decision to grant them residency was made in error.

Continue reading...
title: ‘We’ve done everything by the book’: EU citizens left in limbo after UK government strips post-Brexit residency status

author: Robert Tait in Washington
description:
President has let rip with swearwords in recent months, redefining norms about acceptable language in public office

With a lifetime of political memories stretching back to John F Kennedy’s assassination and the Black civil rights struggles of the 1960s, Cheryl Johnson had one complaint above all else about today’s politicians: the swearing.

“All this cursing in politics, we never heard that before,” said Johnson, a retired social worker living in the Pittsburgh area. “Words are very powerful, and the past 45 presidents of this country, have not used such vile language.

Continue reading...
title: Bad language: profane Trump brings presidential swearing out into open

author: As told to Rich Pelley
description:
The Pussycat Doll went roller skating to the Beach Boys and is ‘completely over’ Gangnam Style. But what song makes her cry every time?

The first song I fell in love with
When I learned to drive and got my first car, I felt this real freedom. I’d put the windows down, blare out Ghetto Supastar (That Is What You Are) by Pras, featuring Ol’ Dirty Bastard and Mýa, and sing at the top of my lungs.

The first single I bought
Every Friday night we’d go to the roller skating rink, and I couldn’t wait for them to play Kokomo by the Beach Boys, from the Cocktail soundtrack. So I bought it on cassette from Best Buy in Warrensburg, Missouri.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Eminem’s Lose Yourself is my anthem for getting the kids out of the house’: Kimberly Wyatt’s honest playlist

author: Felicity Cloake
description:
While it’s ideal for mopping up chilli and soup, this Southern US staple can be made substantial enough for a main meal with a few simple additions

Like banana bread, a rather less ancient North American creation, cornbread isn’t a loaf in the conventional sense. Though it’s perfect for soaking up chilli, brothy bean soups and the like, it’s actually substantial enough to be the main event, rather than something you might reach for to mop the plate after it. (It’s also gluten-free, should that be a consideration.)

Prep 10 min
Soak 2 hr
Cook 25 min
Serves 6

Continue reading...
title: How to make cornbread – recipe | Felicity Cloake's masterclass

author: George Chidi
description:
Fears grow that loyalists in key states could use critical period when votes are counted to amplify false claims

Election experts have warned Donald Trump’s administration could use the crucial hours and days after November’s midterm elections to disrupt the results after struggling to enforce a crackdown on voting.

With less than six weeks remaining until polls close, and control of US Congress in the balance, the post-election “counting window” is seen as as a particularly vulnerable moment by former US federal government officials.

Continue reading...
title: Trump allies could use midterms ‘counting window’ to disrupt results, experts warn

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Microsoft co-founder and philanthropist speaks with NBC’s Kristen Welker in interview airing on Sunday

Bill Gates has called on the US’s federal legislators and law enforcers to regulate the development of artificial intelligence (AI), saying in an interview airing on Sunday that the technology left unchecked could cause “a billion deaths” and “no one thinks self-regulation is enough”.

“You need law enforcement and the politicians to get into the discussion about what safeguards and monitoring look like,” the Microsoft co-founder and philanthropist said to Kristen Welker, the NBC Meet the Press host. “And that has to be a required thing.”

Continue reading...
title: Bill Gates says unchecked AI could ‘cause a billion deaths’ in call for regulation

author: Chloe Mac Donnell
description:
Critics say partnership between Mounjaro maker Eli Lilly and fashion giant suggests thinness is an aspiration

The fifth iteration of Vogue World, overseen by Anna Wintour, took place in Milan on Tuesday night. Gigi Hadid and Jennifer Lopez provided theatrics on the catwalk, but it was one of the event’s backers that caused the biggest stir.

Eli Lilly, an American pharmaceutical company that manufactures a wide range of medicines, including weight-loss jabs Mounjaro and the Foundayo pill, was listed in the event credits as one of its “fashion adjacent” sponsors.

Continue reading...
title: ‘It’s problematic’: concern as weight-loss jab maker sponsors Vogue World event

author: Ruby Tandoh
description:
It has taken me decades to get over the vegetarian cookbooks of my past

It would be unwise to overstate things, the world being as it is, but what happened in the UK with stuffed peppers is a tragedy. You know the ones I mean: traffic light bell peppers stuffed with a cupboard raid of rice, breadcrumbs, lentils, nuts and veg – 70s stuffed peppers. The kind you might find in a wholefoods cookbook, cheerfully distended and jaunty of cap, with the physiognomy of PC Plod. I used to make them at university sometimes, my sensibilities being, as ever, several decades out of touch. I think I was trying to channel the vegetarian cookbooks my parents once had – in the years before discovering pesto, these peppers were the vegetarian’s lot. The recipes I concocted bore things like buckwheat groats, curly leaf parsley and yeast extract. To this day, I cannot hear “stuffed vegetables” without flashbacks to such peppers and their generous cargo of junk.

It’s a shame, because stuffed
title: ‘I cannot hear “stuffed vegetables” without flashbacks’

author: Dale Berning Sawa; photographs by Kate Peters
description:
The Londoner is the set designer big names turn to for eye-popping spectacle. As a new retrospective opens, she gives the Guardian a glimpse at her studio

Four years ago, the V&A East Storehouse in east London got in touch with Es Devlin. The museum’s curators wanted to invite the British artist and designer to respond to a 100-year-old theatrical backdrop by the Russian artist and designer Natalia Goncharova. For a 1926 London production of The Firebird by the Ballets Russes, Goncharova had painted a fortified Muscovite cityscape festooned with onion domes and spires, rust-red and golden against a deep-blue sky. Devlin didn’t know much about Goncharova. But alighting on the term she had favoured for describing her kaleidoscopic approach to art-making, Devlin realised she’d found a kindred spirit. “She called herself an ‘everythingist’,” Devlin says, a smile in her eyes.

Works in progress in Devlin’s studio
title: ‘I’m an everythingist’: How Es Devlin became the go-to for Beyoncé gigs, fashion runways and the Olympics

author: Hannah Ewens
description:
As a journalist, I’m endlessly curious about people – or I was until short-form video made real-life interactions feel like a drag

It’s never pleasant to confront something unflattering about yourself, particularly when you catch yourself in the act. Recently I was mid-conversation with a stranger at a party, when I suddenly became conscious of my internal monologue: yes, hurry up, get to the point, you’re going to say this, then that, and what is the takeaway here?

This wasn’t the first time I had noticed a shift in my real-life interactions. Over the preceding months, I had felt tired, even irritated, when loved ones so much as veered close to an anecdote or detail about their lives that I thought I had already heard. During interviews I conducted as a journalist, it sometimes took a heroic effort to concentrate on conversations once they failed to be truly stimulating. Ordinarily I am endlessly curious about people, but I couldn’t ignore a creeping
title: My Instagram reels addiction has ruined my ability to have a conversation. But can I get it back? | Hannah Ewens

author: Chris Osuh Community affairs correspondent
description:
A new walking heritage trail follows hidden histories and overlooked landmarks in a city built on the cotton trade

  • All photographs by Ruby Ramelize

They are the stories that have survived decades, despite being largely ignored by official acts of commemoration, obscured, or erased from the landscape. Now, chapters from Manchester’s Black history are being brought to life by a series of walking tours in the city, led by local historians, including Linford Sweeney, the Moss Side-raised genealogist, and the urbanist Hayley Flynn.

The Heritage in Action trail – guided walks exploring the lives of people whose labour made the city what it is and the city’s direct relationship with transatlantic slavery – will run in the city on 7 October, World Cotton Day. The events have been produced by the Guardian’s Legacies of Enslavement programme and the charity Greater Manchester Moving, which works to improve the region’s wellbeing through physical activity.<
title: Giving voice to a lost history: retracing the steps of the Black lives that shaped Manchester

author: Olivia Petter, Derek Owusu, William Rayfet Hunter, Poorna Bell, Annie Lord and Nikesh Shukla
description:
From making life hell for a young teacher to doubting the motives of a caring foster mother, Olivia Petter, Derek Owusu, Annie Lord and other writers repent for past bad behaviour

At school, I was not a good girl. Actually, that’s putting it mildly: I was an emotional terrorist hellbent on inflicting torture and humiliation on my year 6 teacher, Ms Hill, one whoopee cushion at a time. That’s how it began, anyway, but like all crimes, mine followed a strategic pattern of escalation, carefully executed alongside my best friend and accomplice.

Continue reading...
title: ‘I’d like to explain why I was such a monster back then’: six writers on the apologies they wish they’d made

author: Richard Partington in Warsaw
description:
In the first article in a series on the Polish economy, we look at the country’s defence boom and its implications

A short distance north from Warsaw along the Vistula river, camouflaged missile launchers roll through the quiet village of Czosnów.

As recently as two years ago, their destination – a hi-tech weapons facility opened this month – had been a cornfield. Now, as Poland drives up defence investment at one of the fastest rates in the developed world, this rural spot has been transformed amid Europe’s response to Russian aggression and US disengagement.

Continue reading...
title: Poland is racing ahead with military spending – but will it help or damage its economic growth story?

author: Rob Evans
description:
Officer forced to admit relationship with woman lasting at least six months while working under fake name Dave Evans

An undercover police officer who infiltrated leftwing and animal rights campaign groups appears to have lied to the spycops inquiry when he claimed he did not have a sexual relationship as part of his deployment.

The officer who used the fake name Dave Evans had originally testified that he did not have any relationships while using his fake identity.

Continue reading...
title: Undercover police officer lied to spycops inquiry about sexual relationship

author: Deborah Cole in Salzburg
description:
Sixty years after the film’s release, Salzburg is embracing a Hollywood classic it once kept at arm’s length

Let’s start at the very beginning – famously, a very good place to start.

Just two decades after the second world war, a Hollywood crew descended on Salzburg with stars, show tunes and a compelling, essentially true story of love and opposition to Adolf Hitler: The Sound of Music.

Kym Karath, Debbie Turner, Angela Cartwright, Duane Chase, Heather Menzies, Nicholas Hammond, Charmian Carr and Julie Andrews in The Sound Of Music.

Continue reading...
title: ‘A joyful place’: a new museum coaxes Austrians to embrace The Sound of Music

author: David Harewood
description:
I understand the pressure on the public purse, but I have also seen the effect of our spending on the ground. Our choices can do so much good

  • David Harewood is a Unicef UK ambassador

As Labour party conference approaches, politicians will debate spending priorities, fiscal pressures and the UK’s place in the world. Before those discussions begin, I want ministers to picture a hospital ward I visited in Sierra Leone with Unicef (United Nations Children’s Fund).

Inside the special-care baby unit at Makeni regional hospital were rows of tiny premature babies, some no bigger than my hand. Around them stood dedicated nurses and anxious parents, all willing these newborns to survive.

David Harewood is a Unicef UK ambassador

Continue reading...
title: I have seen with pride how British overseas aid saves children’s lives. That is why I say cuts should be reversed | David Harewood

author: Amelia Hill
description:
Financial pressures, legal changes and shifting attitudes may help explain why couples are staying married for longer

“We don’t know anyone whose marriage hit the skids after just a few years,” Celia said, reflecting on her divorce. “Everyone seemed to cling on to their relationships for as long as they possibly could.”

It took Celia two years to initiate divorce after realising her 12-year marriage wasn’t going anywhere – and the latest figures show this experience is increasingly common, with marriages that end in divorce now lasting longer than at any point since records began.

Continue reading...
title: ‘I turbocharged my career then pressed eject’: why couples are getting divorced later

author: Annalisa Barbieri
description:
You really need to find a way to talk about this and explore the underlying issues – for both of you

Since the start of our relationship, more than 20 years ago, I was aware my husband had a strong work ethic.

But I am beginning to resent the time he spends working, which often includes late nights and weekends when an emergency happens.

Continue reading...
title: My husband never stops working, but he won’t discuss it. Should I leave him?

author: Guardian Staff
description:
Authorities declared a flood disaster across Bangkok after almost two days of heavy rain left homes, shops and roads waterlogged and residents wading through waist-deep water.

The Thai capital recorded 300mm of rainfall over 48 hours through ⁠Saturday in some areas, flooding roads and ​leaving ​some cars ​submerged. The rain swelled the city’s network of canals, sending murky water into surrounding homes, restaurants and shops

Continue reading...
title: Bangkok’s flood disaster – in pictures

author: Jesse Hassenger
description:
New York film festival: The follow-up to 2023’s Oscar-winning Godzilla Minus One dazzles with smart social commentary and jaw-dropping effects

Even by the standards of older movie stars catching a major second wind later in their careers, Godzilla pulled off an impressive reclamation of the spotlight three years ago. Godzilla Minus One, the most recent reboot featuring the 70-year-old kaiju – the version(s) from his native Japan, mind, not the Americanized one concurrently starring in a series of Warner Bros blockbusters opposite King Kong – wasn’t just another monster-movie success. It fully crossed over, becoming the highest-grossing Japanese-language movie ever released in North America, and won an Academy Award to boot for i
title: Godzilla Minus Zero review – spectacular Japanese action continues franchise’s winning streak
